docs.title: DocManaga Developer Portal
docs.text:
Welcome to the DocManaga Developer Platform.

DocManaga allows developers to integrate secure document management into their applications and continuously improve document workflows across enterprise systems.

This portal gives your team everything needed to build production-ready integrations: API references, onboarding guides, authentication patterns, error handling examples, and operational best practices.

docs.title: Why Build With DocManaga
docs.text:
• Reduce manual document handling with API-driven workflows
  • Centralize uploads, retrieval, sharing, and lifecycle controls
  • Improve security with token authentication, access control, and password-protected sharing
  • Scale enterprise workflows with predictable API behavior and clear integration patterns
  • Accelerate delivery by reusing common document operations across products and teams

docs.title: Developer Benefits
docs.text:
• Faster implementation with straightforward REST endpoints
  • Consistent JSON responses that are easy to parse and validate
  • Clear error codes for better troubleshooting and support automation
  • Endpoint coverage for core operations and advanced features
  • A practical onboarding flow so new developers can go from setup to first integration quickly

docs.title: What This Portal Helps You Build
docs.text:
Example: A procurement platform needs to create purchase-order PDFs, upload them, retrieve them for audit, and share a protected copy with a vendor.

With DocManaga, the platform can:

  1. Create a document record.
  2. Upload the file.
  3. Retrieve metadata and status when needed.
  4. Generate secure links or apply password protection for external sharing.

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• Upload and store documents
  • Secure document sharing
  • Password protection
  • Merge multiple documents
  • Download and manage files

docs.title: Base API URL
docs.text: https://api.docmanaga.com/v1

docs.title: Start Quickly
docs.text:
Follow the onboarding flow in Getting Started to:

  1. Create an API key.

  5. Handle success and error responses.

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text: This guide helps you get from zero to a working DocManaga integration in a few steps.

docs.title: Step 1: Create an API Key
docs.text:
Follow the full setup guide in API Keys.

  1. Sign in to your DocManaga account.
  2. Open the developer settings section.
  3. Generate a new API key for your application environment.
  4. Store it securely (for example, in a secret manager or environment variable).

Recommended environment variable:

DOCMANAGA_API_KEY=YOUR_API_KEY

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
All API requests require an API key.

Use a bearer token in the Authorization header.

Example header:

Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY

docs.title: Base URL
docs.text: https://api.docmanaga.com/v1

docs.title: Step 2: Verify Authentication
docs.text:
curl -X GET https://api.docmanaga.com/v1/documents \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY"

docs.title: Step 3: Upload a Document
docs.text:
curl -X POST https://api.docmanaga.com/v1/documents/upload \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY" \
    -F "file=@invoice.pdf"

Typical success response:

{
    "id": "doc_555",
    "status": "uploaded"
}

docs.title: Step 4: Retrieve a Document
docs.text:
curl -X GET https://api.docmanaga.com/v1/documents/doc_555 \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY"

Typical success response:

{
    "id": "doc_555",
    "name": "invoice.pdf",
    "size": "1.2MB",
    "created_at": "2026-01-10"
}

docs.title: Response Codes and Error Examples
docs.text:
Common status codes:

  • 200 OK: Request successful
  • 201 Created: Resource created successfully
  • 400 Bad Request: Invalid payload or missing required fields
  • 401 Unauthorized: Missing or invalid API key
  • 403 Forbidden: API key lacks required permissions
  • 404 Not Found: Document or endpoint not found
  • 429 Too Many Requests: Rate limit exceeded
  • 500 Internal Server Error: Unexpected server-side failure

Example error response:

{
    "error": {
        "code": "unauthorized",
        "message": "Invalid API key provided."
    }
}

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text:
• Review grouped endpoints in API Reference
  • Use Guides for deeper authentication, upload, and security practices
  • Check SDK Examples for language-specific integration patterns

docs.title: Rate Limits
docs.text: DocManaga enforces request limits to keep the platform reliable and fair for all integrations.

docs.title: Default Limits
docs.text:
• 100 requests per minute per API key
  • 1000 requests per hour per API key
  • Upload-heavy workloads may be subject to additional throughput controls

docs.title: Headers
docs.text:
Rate-limit headers may include:

  • X-RateLimit-Limit
  • X-RateLimit-Remaining
  • X-RateLimit-Reset

docs.title: When You Hit a Limit
docs.text:
If your integration exceeds limits, the API returns 429 Too Many Requests.

Example response:

{
  "error": {
    "code": "rate_limit_exceeded",
    "message": "Too many requests. Retry after 30 seconds."
  }
}

docs.title: Recommended Client Behavior
docs.text:
• Use exponential backoff with jitter.
  • Respect reset hints before retrying.
  • Batch non-urgent operations where possible.
  • Cache document metadata to reduce repeated reads.

docs.title: SDK Examples
docs.text: Use these examples to integrate DocManaga quickly in your preferred language.

docs.title: JavaScript (Node.js)
docs.text:
const API_KEY = process.env.DOCMANAGA_API_KEY;
const BASE_URL = "https://api.docmanaga.com/v1";

async function listDocuments() {
  const response = await fetch(`${BASE_URL}/documents`, {
    headers: {
      Authorization: `Bearer ${API_KEY}`,
    },
  });

  if (!response.ok) {
    throw new Error(`Request failed with ${response.status}`);
  }

  return response.json();
}

docs.title: Python
docs.text:
import os
import requests

API_KEY = os.getenv("DOCMANAGA_API_KEY")
BASE_URL = "https://api.docmanaga.com/v1"

response = requests.get(
    f"{BASE_URL}/documents",
    headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {API_KEY}"},
    timeout=30,
)
response.raise_for_status()
print(response.json())

docs.title: C# (.NET)
docs.text:
using System.Net.Http.Headers;

var apiKey = Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("DOCMANAGA_API_KEY");
var baseUrl = "https://api.docmanaga.com/v1";

using var client = new HttpClient();
client.DefaultRequestHeaders.Authorization =
  new AuthenticationHeaderValue("Bearer", apiKey);

var response = await client.GetAsync($"{baseUrl}/documents");
response.EnsureSuccessStatusCode();

var json = await response.Content.ReadAsStringAsync();
Console.WriteLine(json);

docs.title: Java
docs.text:
import java.net.URI;
import java.net.http.HttpClient;
import java.net.http.HttpRequest;
import java.net.http.HttpResponse;

public class DocManagaExample {
  public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception {
    String apiKey = System.getenv("DOCMANAGA_API_KEY");
    String baseUrl = "https://api.docmanaga.com/v1";

    HttpClient client = HttpClient.newHttpClient();
    HttpRequest request = HttpRequest.newBuilder()
        .uri(URI.create(baseUrl + "/documents"))
        .header("Authorization", "Bearer " + apiKey)
        .GET()
        .build();

    HttpResponse<String> response = client.send(request, HttpResponse.BodyHandlers.ofString());

    if (response.statusCode() >= 200 && response.statusCode() < 300) {
      System.out.println(response.body());
    } else {
      throw new RuntimeException("Request failed with status " + response.statusCode());
    }
  }
}

docs.title: Integration Tips
docs.text:
• Keep API keys in environment variables.
  • Add retry logic for 429 and transient 5xx errors.
  • Validate MIME types and file size before upload.
  • Log request IDs (if provided) for support and troubleshooting.

docs.title: Use Cases
docs.text: The DocManaga API allows developers to build applications that securely store, manage, and share documents. Below are common ways businesses can use the DocManaga platform.

docs.title: Secure Document Storage
docs.text:
Businesses can use the DocManaga API to automatically upload and store important documents such as invoices, contracts, and reports.

For example, a financial application may generate invoices and automatically store them using the Upload Document API.

docs.title: Example Workflow
docs.text:
1. The application generates a PDF invoice.
  2. The application uploads the document using the Upload Document API.
  3. The API returns a document ID.
  4. The document can later be retrieved using the Get Document API.

docs.title: Example Upload Request
docs.text:
curl -X POST https://api.docmanaga.com/v1/documents/upload \
-H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY" \
-F "file=@invoice.pdf"

docs.title: Secure Document Sharing
docs.text:
Businesses can share documents with external users or clients by generating shareable links using the Share Document API.

This is useful for distributing contracts, reports, or any document that needs to be accessed by parties outside the platform.

docs.title: Example Workflow
docs.text:
1. A document is uploaded and stored in DocManaga.
  2. The application calls the Share Document API with the document ID.
  3. The API returns a shareable link.
  4. The link is distributed to the intended recipient.

docs.title: Example Share Request
docs.text:
curl -X POST https://api.docmanaga.com/v1/documents/doc_001/share \
-H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY"

docs.title: Example Response
docs.text:
{
  "share_link": "https://docmanaga.com/share/doc_001"
}

docs.title: API Reference Overview
docs.text: Use this section to discover endpoints by workflow stage and implementation complexity.

docs.title: Core Document Operations
docs.text:
These endpoints support day-to-day document lifecycle management:

  • GET /documents - List documents
  • GET /documents/{id} - Get a specific document
  • POST /documents - Create a document record
  • PUT /documents/{id} - Update document metadata
  • DELETE /documents/{id} - Delete a document

docs.title: File Operations
docs.text:
These endpoints handle binary file transfer:

  • POST /documents/upload - Upload a file
  • GET /documents/{id}/download - Download a file

docs.title: Advanced Features
docs.text:
These endpoints provide enterprise workflow capabilities:

  • POST /documents/{id}/share - Create a shareable link
  • POST /documents/{id}/password - Add or update password protection
  • POST /documents/merge - Merge multiple documents

docs.title: Common Response Patterns
docs.text:
Success responses:

  • 200 OK for successful reads and updates
  • 201 Created for resource creation

Error responses:

  • 400 Bad Request for invalid inputs
  • 401 Unauthorized for invalid/missing API keys
  • 404 Not Found when a document is missing
  • 429 Too Many Requests when rate limits are exceeded

Example error payload:

{
  "error": {
    "code": "validation_error",
    "message": "The field 'name' is required."
  }
}

docs.title: API Keys
docs.text: Use API keys to authenticate every request to the DocManaga API.

docs.title: Create an API Key
docs.text:
1. Sign in to your DocManaga account.
  2. Open developer settings.
  3. Select Create API Key.
  4. Enter a label for your app environment (for example, production-api or staging-api).
  5. Set access scope based on least privilege.
  6. Save and copy the key immediately.

docs.title: Store API Keys Securely
docs.text:
• Store keys in a secret manager or encrypted environment variables.
  • Never commit keys to source control.
  • Do not expose keys in frontend code or public repositories.

Example environment variable:

DOCMANAGA_API_KEY=YOUR_API_KEY

docs.title: Use API Keys in Requests
docs.text:
Send the key in the Authorization header:

Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY

Example request:

curl -X GET https://api.docmanaga.com/v1/documents \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY"

docs.title: Rotate and Revoke Keys
docs.text:
• Rotate keys regularly and during incident response.
  • Revoke unused keys immediately.
  • Use separate keys per environment to reduce blast radius.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
If you receive 401 Unauthorized:

  • Confirm the key value is correct and not expired.
  • Ensure the Authorization header uses Bearer.
  • Verify the key has permission for the requested endpoint.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
All requests to the DocManaga API must be authenticated using an API key.

Authentication ensures that only authorized users can access and manage documents stored in the DocManaga platform.

docs.title: API Keys
docs.text:
When you create a DocManaga developer account, you are issued a unique API key. This key must be included in every request made to the API.

Your API key should be treated as a secret and never exposed publicly.

docs.title: Authorization Header
docs.text:
The API key is sent using the Authorization header in the following format:

Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY

docs.title: Example Request
docs.text:
curl -X GET https://api.docmanaga.com/v1/documents \
-H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY"

docs.title: Security
docs.text: Security is a core component of the DocManaga platform. The API provides several features that help protect sensitive documents and ensure secure access.

docs.title: Password Protection
docs.text:
Developers can protect documents by assigning a password using the Protect Document API.

This feature ensures that only users with the correct password can access the document.

docs.title: Secure Document Sharing
docs.text:
The Share Document API allows developers to generate shareable links that can be distributed to external users.

Share links can include expiration settings to limit access duration.

docs.title: API Key Protection
docs.text:
To prevent unauthorized access:

  • Never expose API keys publicly
  • Store keys in secure environments
  • Use server-side requests whenever possible

docs.title: Encryption
docs.text:
DocManaga ensures documents are encrypted both:

  • In transit using HTTPS
  • At rest within the storage infrastructure

docs.title: Recommended Security Practices
docs.text:
To maximize security when using the API:

  • Implement secure key storage
  • Monitor API usage
  • Regularly audit access permissions
  • Rotate credentials when necessary

docs.title: Uploading Files
docs.text:
DocManaga allows developers to upload and store documents programmatically using the Upload Document API.

This functionality enables businesses to automate document management workflows such as storing invoices, contracts, reports, and other files.

docs.title: Supported File Types
docs.text:
DocManaga supports common file formats including:

  • PDF
  • DOCX
  • TXT
  • CSV
  • JPG
  • PNG

docs.title: Upload Endpoint
docs.text: POST /documents/upload

docs.title: Example Upload Request
docs.text:
curl -X POST https://api.docmanaga.com/v1/documents/upload \
-H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY" \
-F "file=@invoice.pdf"
